mintAuthority.summary: ACRED's working canonical Mint Authority scope is Ethereum only: its token/trust-service master EOA is an uncapped direct issuer and immediate upgrade authority. Avalanche, Ink, Polygon, Solana, and Aptos local issuer and upgrade surfaces are reviewed as bridge-representation controls under bridgeRouteRisk pending proof of independent reconciled fund liabilities; they are not additional canonical Mint Authority.

upgradeability.controlRef: ACRED Ethereum master and upgrade owner

controls.label: ACRED Ethereum master and upgrade owner
controls.evidence: At the fixed exact cutoff, this zero-code EOA was owner or MASTER for the Ethereum ACRED token and trust-service deployments. It could call issueTokens, grant or revoke ISSUER, set the one-time token cap, and immediately replace both Ethereum token or trust-service implementations. cap() returned zero on the Ethereum deployment, which the verified implementation treats as uncapped.

sources.label: BVI FSC - Securitize Tokenized Apollo Diversified Credit Fund

review.evidence: The fixed exact cutoff verified Ethereum as a native ACRED issuance route: its token and trust service share one zero-code EOA owner/MASTER that can issue, administer issuers, set the one-time cap, and upgrade immediately; cap() returned zero and the implementation treats that as uncapped. The launch and Wormhole/Securitize material identify Avalanche, Ink, Polygon, Solana, and Aptos as cross-chain destinations, while current destination controls remain adverse bridge-representation facts. Public primary sources do not prove that those five local issuance surfaces create independently reconciled fund liabilities or are restricted to validated transfer receipts, so they are excluded from canonical Mint Authority and retained under bridgeRouteRisk. Daily Securitize-administered NAV does not establish feeder-token supply-to-assets reconciliation; BVI FSC supervision is established, but reconciliation remains unknown.
